source.title: On Learning-Curve Monotonicity for Maximum Likelihood Estimators

record.tranche_reason: The study derives new theoretical results refining the data-monotonicity question: forward-KL risk strictly decreases with sample size in specified well-specified MLE families. It does not test double descent in deep networks or near their interpolation threshold.
record.gate_note: The paper's discussion of double descent cites prior work and describes it as largely orthogonal; those cited results are not rows. The rows below are the paper's own learning-curve results.
record.test_reason: The study proves learning-curve monotonicity for well-specified parametric MLEs, measured by KL risk. It has no overparameterized or interpolating regime: below the thresholds n ≤ d+1 or d+2 the risk is infinite. So it says nothing about whether more data hurts near an interpolation threshold (V3), and it tests no other version. The authors call double descent 'largely orthogonal' to their focus. Strict decrease above the parameter-count threshold, with divergence at it, is also what double-descent theory predicts on the underparameterized side. The results are therefore not evidence against V3, and the record's limits_scope label on V3 should be dropped.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. The authors prove forward-KL data monotonicity, in fact complete monotonicity, for MLEs of Gaussians with unknown covariance (known or unknown mean) and of Gamma distributions with unknown scale. They prove reverse-KL monotonicity for general regular exponential families. They describe double descent as largely orthogonal to their well-specified parametric focus.
record.recipe_differences: The study proves analytical monotonicity results for parametric MLE learning curves measured by KL divergence; it does not reproduce the original deep-network/model-size experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: For well-specified MLEs, expected forward-KL risk strictly decreases, and is completely monotone, in n above the finiteness threshold. This holds for Gaussian covariance estimation with known or unknown mean (Theorems 1.1 and 1.2) and for Gamma scale estimation (Theorem 1.3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Learning curves of well-specified parametric MLEs under log loss are monotone, indeed completely monotone, in sample size.

fits_no_version.finding: Expected reverse-KL risk of the MLE is nonincreasing in n for regular exponential families, and strictly decreasing under the stated conditions. Explicit Gaussian formulas are also given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In regular exponential families, the MLE's expected reverse-KL risk does not increase with sample size.

record.problems: The results are theoretical and confined to specified well-specified parametric MLE settings; the study does not evaluate deep networks, the interpolation-threshold regime, or empirical test error in the original settings.

untested.parts: No overparameterized or interpolating regime is studied. Risk is infinite below the n ≈ d threshold, so whether more samples hurt near interpolation is not examined.
No label noise, regularization, or multiple peaks.

record.verdict_notes: The authors remark that their Gaussian result covers high-dimensional linear regression with Gaussian covariates, so its MLE log-loss is data-monotone. This holds only where n exceeds the dimension threshold, where risk is finite. It does not address the n < p interpolating regime where sample-wise double descent appears. The proofs are reported to be AI-generated (GPT-5.2 Pro) and verified by the human authors. The paper is a preprint.

versions.untested_parts: Training epochs or training time are not varied.
The original deep-network settings and the region near their interpolation threshold are not tested; the study gives theoretical results for specified parametric MLE families instead.
No general double-descent curve across model classes is tested.
No common effective-complexity measure across size, epochs, or samples is tested.
The effects of label noise, regularization, or multiple peaks are not tested.
Complexity is not recounted using an effective number of parameters.

rows.subject: centered multivariate Gaussian with unknown covariance
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluate forward-KL MLE risk as sample size n increases.

conditions.value: risk is infinite for n ≤ d + 1; finite and strictly decreasing for n > d + 1

rows.measure: Expected forward KL divergence from the true Gaussian to the fitted Gaussian
rows.value: For n > d + 1, E_n,d(Σ*) = 1/2(f_d(n) − d), independent of Σ*, and E_n+1,d(Σ*) < E_n,d(Σ*). For n ≤ d + 1, E_n,d(Σ*) = +∞. The risk function is also shown to be completely monotone.
rows.note: Analytical result for the stated Gaussian MLE family; it does not establish behavior near a deep-network interpolation threshold.
rows.check: This is forward-KL monotonicity in a well-specified Gaussian covariance MLE. Risk is infinite for n ≤ d+1, so there is no regime near or below the threshold where more data could hurt. It does not measure V3's effect, so it should not be linked to V3 or marked reversed.

rows.subject: full multivariate Gaussian model with unknown mean and covariance
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluate forward-KL MLE risk as sample size n increases.

conditions.value: risk is infinite for n ≤ d + 2; finite and strictly decreasing for n > d + 2

rows.measure: Expected forward KL divergence from the true Gaussian to the fitted Gaussian
rows.value: For n > d + 2, E_n,d^full(μ*, Σ*) = 1/2(g_d(n) − d), independent of (μ*, Σ*), and E_n+1,d^full(μ*, Σ*) < E_n,d^full(μ*, Σ*). For n ≤ d + 2, E_n,d^full(μ*, Σ*) = +∞. The risk function is also shown to be completely monotone.
rows.note: Analytical result for the stated Gaussian MLE family.
rows.check: Same issue as r1, for the unknown-mean Gaussian; risk is infinite for n ≤ d+2. It does not measure V3's interpolation-threshold effect.

rows.subject: Gamma distribution with unknown scale and known shape
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluate forward-KL MLE risk as sample size n increases.

conditions.value: risk is infinite if nα ≤ 1; finite and strictly decreasing if nα > 1

rows.measure: Expected forward KL divergence from the true Gamma distribution to the fitted Gamma distribution
rows.value: For nα > 1, risk is h_α(n) = α[ψ(nα) − log(nα) + 1/(nα − 1)] and is strictly decreasing in n; for nα ≤ 1, the expectation is +∞. The risk function is also shown to be completely monotone.
rows.note: The α = 1 case is identified as scale estimation for exponential random variables.
rows.check: This is a one-parameter Gamma scale MLE with no capacity or interpolation threshold. It does not bear on V3, so 'reversed' is not appropriate.

rows.subject: regular exponential families
rows.operation_detail: Prove a sample-size monotonicity result for expected reverse-KL risk of the MLE.

conditions.value: exists and lies in the interior for each n in the range considered
strict convexity of A* on M and non-degenerate T(X)

rows.measure: Expected reverse KL divergence from the fitted distribution to the true distribution
rows.value: Expected reverse-KL risk is nonincreasing with n; it is strictly decreasing under the stated strict-convexity and non-degeneracy conditions.
rows.note: Reverse KL is not the forward-KL/test-loss measure named by V3; recorded as a related result outside the listed versions.
rows.check: Reverse-KL monotonicity in exponential families; correctly linked to no version.

rows.subject: centered multivariate Gaussian with unknown covariance
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluate reverse-KL MLE risk as sample size n increases.

conditions.value: risk is infinite for n < d; formula and strict decrease for n ≥ d

rows.measure: Expected reverse KL divergence from the fitted Gaussian to the true Gaussian
rows.value: For n ≥ d, risk is 1/2 r_d(n), where r_d(n) = d log(n/2) − Σ_{j=1}^d ψ((n − j + 1)/2), and it is strictly decreasing in n. For n < d, the expectation is +∞.
rows.note: Reverse-KL risk, rather than forward-KL test loss.

rows.subject: full multivariate Gaussian model with unknown mean and covariance
rows.operation_detail: Analytically evaluate reverse-KL MLE risk as sample size n increases.

conditions.value: risk is infinite for n ≤ d; formula and strict decrease for n ≥ d + 1

rows.measure: Expected reverse KL divergence from the fitted Gaussian to the true Gaussian
rows.value: For n ≥ d + 1, risk is 1/2 r_d(n − 1), with r_d as defined for the known-mean case, and it is strictly decreasing in n. For n ≤ d, the expectation is +∞.
rows.note: Reverse-KL risk, rather than forward-KL test loss.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: The studied well-specified Gaussian and Gamma MLE families, above their stated finiteness thresholds
reader_labels.reason: In these settings, forward-KL risk strictly decreases as more samples are used, rather than rising; this qualifies applicability but does not test the deep-network interpolation regime (r1–r3).
